pr_title: sql: look up schemas on database for negative name resolution
pr_body:
See individual commits for details.

Closes #53301.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/53290)
First 2 commits are ready for review, if you want.
Tagging Paul for commit 1. (I also reordered the commits, so the sql-related ones are 2 and 3). This still needs a test for the cleanup on failed restore case, but I think it's ready for a look.

> +1 to doing this in `publishDescriptors` - unfortunately we still need to be careful about cleaning this up (like is currently done) in case of an error between marking the descriptors public and actually finishing the job.

Hmm, I would really like to not have the database descriptor map get out of sync with the schema namespace entries if at all possible. (It would also make it annoying if in the future, as is my hope, we start enforcing the invariant on writes.) I'm open to this as a short-term solution, but it seems to me like the best way to do this is to also call `PublishMultiple` (or equivalent) at the start of the job to update the type backreferences and the databases (and also creating all the descriptors in the same transaction). Would it be acceptable if we just left the type and database updates the way they are, and come back later to clean them up?
For what it's worth, I've gathered up all the improvements discussed in this review (and others) into a meta-issue for future work, some of which I expect to be done for 20.2: #53378

> A test for the cleanup would be nice - backup tests have simulated a bad backup by removing the SSTs (https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/pkg/ccl/backupccl/backup_test.go#L1691).

I tacked on a check toward the end of the existing test. Let me try to expand on it a bit.

I don't really have much to add, but the discussions above all sound right, and I'm also a proponent of adding an OFFLINE state to these descriptors so that we have more flexibility while mucking around with them during restores.

@ajwerner Yeah, I think I'm on board with that prioritized list. I could maybe live without fixing all the descriptor accesses in full generality for 20.2, but in principle it shouldn't be too hard.

Here's that meta-issue for RESTORE improvements again (posting where it's easier to see): #53378

review_comments: Is it valid to add the table descriptors (even if offline) but not add the types they reference at the same time?
hmm, probably not. We need to have those backreferences there to avoid dropping the type as soon as we add the table descriptor to the database.
was this a bug that this wasn't happening before
It was happening before (above). I just moved it to a separate function.
It doesn't seem like there is anything we can do about this without introducing that extra lookup right?
Sorry, what do you mean by "this"?

Yeah, I don't think there's a way to completely eliminate this. We could maybe purge old leases for the database descriptor whenever we do it for the schema, but that still doesn't provide a guarantee.
